title: Whole-tower adjunct characterization of the specified integral comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $R_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}=\lim_m(A_{E,m})_T$ for $T=X,Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and use module sheaves and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\operatorname{Tow}_X=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ and let $\Delta$ be the termwise constant-tower functor [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. For a strict tower complex $T_\bullet$, choose a K-injective tower resolution $j_T:T_\bullet\to J_\bullet$ with injective terms [def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-sp-injective-resolutions], compute $R\lim T_\bullet=\lim J_\bullet$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], and put $\epsilon_T=[j_T]^{-1}\circ[\Delta\lim J_\bullet\to J_\bullet]$. Then for every $H\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ the map
$$\Phi_{H,T}:\operatorname{Hom}(H,R\lim T_\bullet)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta H,T_\bullet),\qquad f\longmapsto\epsilon_T\circ\Delta(f)$$
is a bijection, natural in both derived variables and independent of the resolution.
For $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], let $q:P\to K$ be the chosen flat-term K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Set $P_m=P\otimes_{R_Y}(A_{E,m})_Y$, $C_{g,m}=\operatorname{Res}_m g_m^*P_m$, with the actual quotient transitions, and $\theta_{g,m}:g^{-1}P\to C_{g,m}$, $x\mapsto\bar x\otimes1$; these are the objects, coefficient actions and units of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b). Let $\theta_g^\Delta:\Delta g^{-1}P\to C_{g,\bullet}$ be this strict family and identify the specified cone model of $Lg^*K$ with $R\lim C_{g,\bullet}$ by the normalized Roos comparison [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. The specified comparison $\kappa^g_K$ of that definition is characterized uniquely by
$$\epsilon_{C_g}\circ\Delta(\kappa^g_K)=\theta_g^\Delta\circ\Delta[g^{-1}(q)]^{-1}.$$
In particular the zero shifted-product cone lift $z\mapsto(0,(\theta_{g,m}(z))_m)$, conjugated by $[g^{-1}(q)]^{-1}$ and by the normalized Roos identification, is the morphism with this entire-tower adjunct.

proof.text: Use the already constructed integralComparisonConstantAdjunction of def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models. Its inverse Hom equivalence is exactly f mapped by the derived constant tower functor and then composed with integralComparisonTowerCounit. Hence this map is bijective on arbitrary derived variables. Functoriality and counit naturality give the displayed two-variable naturality equation. For every quasi-isomorphism j:T to I, counit naturality followed by the inverse of Q(j) transports integralComparisonTowerCounit_computes from I to T, proving the every-resolution formula.

For any strict tower augmentation theta:Delta V to C and zero-shifted-coordinate lift z:V to Roos(C), choose a K-injective resolution j:C to I. The ordinary adjunction lifted to complexes gives a:V to lim I whose constant-tower composite with the ordinary counit is theta followed by j. Thus a followed by the nth limit projection is theta_n followed by j_n. The defining properties of integralComparisonLimitToRoos give its limit projections and zero shifted component. Factor a zero-shifted-coordinate map through the unshifted cone inclusion using the two-coordinate identity. The signed cocone map preserves that inclusion, so product extensionality and the projection equations prove z followed by Roos(j) equals a followed by integralComparisonLimitToRoos(I), as an equality of strict chain maps.

Naturality of the given normalized Roos isomorphism rho and its computes field turn the preceding strict identity into Q(z) followed by rho_C inverse followed by Rlim(Q(j)) followed by rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso(I).hom equals Q(a). The normalization also makes Q(integralComparisonLimitToRoos(I)) invertible, since its composite with the right-derived comparison is rho_I. Use the K-injective counit formula, its naturality along Q(j), and naturality of mapDerivedCategoryFactors to identify the whole-tower adjunct of Q(z) followed by rho_C inverse with Q(theta), after the canonical exact-derived factor. Cancel Q(j). No equality is inferred by derived projections alone.

Specialize to the actual pullback strict tower, thetaStrictTower and inverseImageRoosComparisonComplex. The mapping-cocone lift equations give its theta_n product coordinates and zero shifted coordinate. Unfold inverseImagePullbackComparison and integralComparisonPullbackLimitIso and cancel their mutually inverse representative isomorphisms; this proves the second displayed cone formula. Precompose the preceding whole-tower adjunct identity by the localized inverse-image resolution denominator and use functoriality of the constant tower functor. Finally, injectivity of its counit Hom map and cancellation of integralComparisonPullbackLimitIso prove the requested if and only if.

Step 2: in Stacks 0FND/0DVC (derived.tex l.9517/9570) and lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general the roles are reversed: their A=Tow, B=Mod, F=lim, G=Δ. Step 3: the fraction formula with s=j, t=id, f=id gives a_h(id)=e_J, so e(id)=[j]^{-1}[e_J]=ε_T. Functoriality with l=Δ(m) gives Φ. Taking s=j' gives independence of the resolution. Step 6: precomposing with Δ[g^{-1}q]^{-1} and using the bijection at H=g^{-1}K gives uniqueness. Edge cases checked: K=0, a constant tower, g=id (gives the completion map) and unbounded H.
